item.content:encoded:

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s
answers to questions
from Izvestia regarding Montenegro’s introduction of a visa regime for Russian citizens
(October 14, 2026)
❓
Question: Previously, the Montenegrin authorities announced the introduction of
a visa regime for Russian citizens
effective November 1. Has the Montenegrin side provided any clarifications in this regard? How will this decision affect relations between Moscow and Podgorica? Are any retaliatory measures planned?
Maria Zakharova:
Yes, on September 28, the Montenegrin Foreign Ministry notified the Russian Side of
the termination
of
the Agreement between the Government of the Russian Federation and the Government of Montenegro on the terms of reciprocal travel for citizens
of September 24, 2008.
According to the clarifications received, in practice this means that, from November 1,
our citizens will only be able to enter Montenegro and stay in the country with a visa
. Accordingly,
Montenegrin citizens will also have to obtain visas to travel to Russia
.
❗️
Podgorica’s decision obviously damages Montenegro’s own interests.
The groundwork laid over many years in Russian-Montenegrin relations is being consistently dismantled to cater to European aspirations
, and due attention is not being paid to the economic consequences of such steps.
Undoubtedly, the introduction of a visa regime will
reduce the tourist flow from Russia
,
damage Montenegrin businesse
s and
worsen the investment climate
. At the same time, it is, of course, pointless for the Montenegrin authorities to count on any compensation from Brussels for the inevitable losses.
***
❓
Question: It has recently emerged that the EU has begun drawing up clear, phased plans for the accession of Albania, Moldova, Ukraine and Montenegro. At the same time, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia and Serbia also hold EU candidate status in the Balkans. How does Russia view the continuation of European integration of the Balkan countries, given the EU’s drift towards becoming a military bloc?
Maria Zakharova:
How to build relations with the EU is
a sovereign choice for the Balkan countries themselves,
which, incidentally, have been waiting in the queue to join the EU for decades (
Albania
since 2000,
North Macedonia
since 2004,
Montenegro
since 2008, and
Serbia
since 2009).
Over this period, the EU has, of course, changed greatly, and
by no means for the better
. This concerns
both its economic metrics
and
the way it acts on the international stage
.
Frenzied militarisation, a failed migration policy, and a wholly irrational renunciation of trade and energy cooperation with Russia –
all of this has had an extremely negative impact on the socioeconomic situation in Europe
.
The referendum in Iceland in August this year
, in which the island’s population voted against resuming EU membership negotiations,
clearly demonstrated that the EU has lost its appeal.
☝️
The EU’s drift towards becoming a military blo
c, coupled with the declaration of Russia as the principal existential threat for the long term (including “beyond the horizon” of the end of the conflict in and around Ukraine),
has also fundamentally altered the essence of the EU enlargement
. This process no longer in any way implies that new members can retain a neutral status.

item.title: ✊ October 14 – the uprising at the Sobibor Nazi extermination camp – a memorable date in Russia’s military history.
item.description: ✊ October 14 – the uprising at the Sobibor Nazi extermination camp – a memorable date in Russia’s military history. #OTD in 1943 , prisoners at the Sobibor Nazi death camp rose up against their Nazi captors , staging one of the most remarkable acts of resistance during the Holocaust. Located in German-occupied Poland, Sobibor was built for mass extermination . Between 1942 and 1943, at least 167,000 Jews were murdered there . Only a small number of deportees were temporarily spared for forced labour. The uprising was led by Alexander Pechersky, a Soviet officer, together with Leon Feldhendler , a Polish Jewish prisoner who had helped establish the camp’s underground resistance. Pechersky’s military experience and the resolve of his fellow Red Army POWs were crucial to transforming plans for an escape into an organised revolt. ⚔️ On October 14 , the prisoners lured SS personnel into the camp’s workshops, neutralised them and seized their weapons . When the alarm sounded, SS personnel and Ukrainian auxiliary guards opened fire on the prisoners, who broke through barbed wire and crossed minefields in a desperate dash for freedom. item.content:encoded:

✊
October 14 –
the uprising at the Sobibor Nazi extermination camp
– a memorable date in Russia’s military history.
#OTD
in 1943
, prisoners at the Sobibor Nazi death camp rose up against their Nazi captors
, staging one of the most remarkable acts of resistance during the Holocaust.
Located in German-occupied Poland, Sobibor was built for mass extermination
. Between 1942 and 1943,
at least 167,000 Jews were murdered there
. Only a small number of deportees were temporarily spared for forced labour.
The uprising was led by
Alexander Pechersky,
a Soviet officer, together with
Leon Feldhendler
, a Polish Jewish prisoner who had helped establish the camp’s underground resistance.
Pechersky’s military experience and the resolve of his fellow Red Army POWs
were crucial to transforming plans for an escape into an organised revolt.
⚔️
On October 14
,
the prisoners lured SS personnel into the camp’s workshops, neutralised them and seized their weapons
. When the alarm sounded, SS personnel and Ukrainian auxiliary guards opened fire on the prisoners, who broke through barbed wire and crossed minefields in a desperate dash for freedom.
Around 300 Sobibor prisoners managed to escape.
Many were later hunted down and murdered.
Only about 50 of those who escaped survived the war.
Pechersky joined a partisan unit and continued fighting the Nazis.
Following the uprising, the Nazis dismantled Sobibor, seeking to erase the evidence of their crimes
. But the survivors lived to bear witness, preserving the memory of those who never returned.
🕯
We honour the courage of the prisoners who fought for life and freedom, and remember all those murdered at Sobibor.
#Victory81

Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/32750

#WeRemember
📅
#OTD
in 1943, an uprising broke out at
#Sobibor
— the only successful mass escape by POWs from Nazi “death factories” during
#WW2
.
The
Sobibor uprising was helmed by
Alexander Pechersky,
a Soviet POW, lieutenant of the Red Army, held among others in Sobibor. The
Soviet officer performed a truly heroic feat
— just in a few weeks, he managed to devise an escape plan, rally other prisoners and inspired them to fight the Nazis.
◼️
During
#WWII
, Germany established around 14'000 'death camps'. Among them, the so-called
death factories
became infamous as places where the Nazis herded their victims
for the one purpose — annihilation.
Sobibor was among such “death factory”, established in the south-east of Nazi-occupied Poland, near the Western Bug River and the Polish-Soviet border. The camp was built alongside the railway line between the towns of Chełm and Włodawa.
POWs were transported to Sobibor in entire railway carriages,
for one sole purpose — to be killed
. The camp was turned into a veritable 'assembly line' for the
mass murder of human beings.
Each and every day, up to six trains carrying POWs arrived at Sobibor, including prisoners of war and civilians — elderly people, women and children.
At Sobibor, the Nazis
starved their victims and exploited them to death
. Inhuman medical experiments were conducted on POWs. People from
Austria
,
Czechoslovakia
,
France
and other countries were brought to the camp to be tortured. In June 1943, two special trains carrying children arrived at Sobibor from the
Netherlands
. In September 1943, a group of Soviet POWs arrived from the Minsk transit camp.
According to various estimates, the Nazis exterminated up to 250'000 POWs at Sobibor during the camp’s existence.
🎖
From the all-Union newspaper '
Krasnaya Armiya
' (
The Red Army
)
(September 2, 1944):
The Nazis turned Poland into one vast prison, where millions of people from every country in Europe perished after indescribable suffering.
<...>
The Sobibor camp was one of the death factories established by the Germans on Polish territory. Residents of the Polish village of Zhlobok-2 <...> wrote in a letter to the Red Army command that the inhabitants of villages neighbouring Sobibor knew well of the conditions in this horrific concentration camp.
Every day, more than 1'000 people of various nationalities were exterminated in the camp’s gas chambers. <...>
The Germans referred to this camp as a “button factory” and a “thread factory”...
***
⚔️
On 14 October 1943, an uprising broke out at Sobibor under the leadership of lieutenant
Alexander Pechersky.
The POWs, who dared to challenge the enemy,
engaged in an unequal battle
. Overpowering 'SS' guards with their bare hands, prisoners rushed towards the main gate despite machine-gun fire from the watchtowers.
❗️
Nothing could stop exhausted people determined to break free from Nazi enslavement.
As a result of the uprising, around 300 people managed to
escape from the sheer hell on earth
. Many of those who survived and made it to freedom joined the resistance movement and continued fighting the Nazis.
Pechersky himself joined the Belarusian partisans
and, in 1944, returned to the front, fighting the enemy as part of an assault battalion.
The
#
SobiborUprising
became a testament to the unbending human will and strength of spirit — a symbol of
the triumph of good over Nazi evil
.
The crimes committed at Sobibor formed part of the charges brought against the Nazis at the
Nuremberg Trials
.
In March 1962, eleven guards who had served at
Sobibor
and
Treblinka
stood trial in Kiev. Alexander Pechersky himself testified as a witness.
All the Nazi criminals were sentenced to death.
Today, the
Alexander Pechersky Foundation
, together with the
Russian Military Historical Society
, museums and other organisations, is doing everything possible to ensure that the
memory of the heroic feat
of the Sobibor prisoners is
carefully preserved
and passed on to future generations.
#LestWeForget
#Victory81

item.title: 🎙 Remarks by Russia’s Ambassador to Australia Mikhail Petrakov on the Australian media’s coverage of the Ukraine conflict
item.description: 🎙 Remarks by Russia’s Ambassador to Australia Mikhail Petrakov on the Australian media’s coverage of the Ukraine conflict (14 October 2026) 💬 We have been witnessing what looks like a well-organised campaign in the Australian media against the Russia-US arrangement on diesel sales. The media and various experts portray the neo-Nazi Kiev regime as a “dove of peace” , seeking de-escalation and a diplomatic settlement – and hence, in the Western logic, in need of more weapons and military assistance. <…> ☝️ For when we call it neo-Nazi , it is not a figure of speech . It was this particular type of extremists who came to power in Kiev following the violent coup d’état in 2014 . The regime started spreading Nazi ideology, destroying everything Russian , killing thousands of Russians in Donbass , in the war which lasted eight years, until the special military operation began. The Belgian diplomat was informed that the Russian Side resolutely rejects the increasingly frequent and wholly unfounded assertions by the Kingdom’s military and political leadership concerning growing hybrid and sabotage threats, alongside direct military threats to Belgium and Europe purportedly emanating from Russia. It was emphasised that the overtly aggressive statements by certain representatives of the Belgian authorities, who deliberately portray Russia as an enemy, contribute to a further escalation and increase the risk of the confrontation they are stoking spiralling out of control. ❗️ The Belgian Side was urged to consider the consequences of such statements and to rein in its anti-Russian rhetoric , which is fuelling a further rise in tensions on the European continent.

🇷🇺
🎙
Comment by Russian Ambassador to the Netherlands H.E. V.Tarabrin for
TASS
regarding the refusal to issue visas to several Russian female athletes seeking to participate in the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Rotterdam
🔹
We received this information with outrage.
By deliberately denying visas to our top gymnasts seeking to
participate in the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships (Rotterdam, October 17-25, 2026), the Dutch authorities have once again demonstrated their utter disregard for one of the fundamental principles of international sport - fair play. This is clearly a deliberate attempt to weaken our team through political and bureaucratic means.
🔹
I personally visited the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs
, where I strongly urged the authorities to honour their obligations as the host country of an international sport event and ensure that all Russian gymnasts receive the necessary documents to participate.
🔹
Instead, I was presented with utterly unconvincing arguments that defy any reasonable criticism. We were told that visa applications would supposedly be assessed by the Netherlands in light of the "potential negative impact of the participation of Russian champions on international relations". Such position is simply impossible to justify or explain in any rational terms.
🔹
With this decision, The Hague has not only discredited itself
by denying entry to Angelina Melnikova, Viktoria Listunova and Anna Kalmykova, but has also put the organisers in an extremely difficult position. Without the participation of the strongest athletes, one can hardly speak of a fully representative World Championship. Spectators have been deprived of the opportunity to enjoy performances by internationally acclaimed gymnasts, while athletes from other countries have been denied the chance to test their skills against the true leaders of world gymnastics.
🔹
Ultimately, everyone has lost. The responsibility for casting a shadow over what should be a celebration of sport, bringing people together rather than dividing them, rests entirely with the Dutch authorities. They sought to "teach Russia a lesson", but have only demonstrated that the Netherlands cannot be trusted to host major international sport events.
